chapter_title: The Catechumen asks the Apostle: will Rest come about for Someone who has come out of the Body, if the Saints pray over and make an Alms-offering for him?
chapter_note: The chapter is framed as a catechumen’s question about alms/prayer for the dead; the second half shows strong institutional/pastoral drift (editorial fatigue). The oldest recoverable substrate is preserved mainly in two archetypal “first/second entreaty” cosmological episodes (Mother of Life→Living Spirit; gods→Third Ambassador), plus a fragmented “third entreaty” sequence including Jesus the Splendour as a cosmic being. Later hands repeatedly pivot from cosmos→cosmos narration to cosmos→church practice (elect/catechumens, alms, remembrance, holy church), often as summary/charge paragraphs; a seam-flagged institutional extension appears at ¶42.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic scene-setting (“Once again… our enlightener… congregation”) is hagiographic framing.
Petition/Q&A formula (“I beseech you, my master… recount…”) belongs to the compiling dialogue frame.
Question continues in catechumen voice; doctrinal tension posed, not cosmological exposition.
Reiterated request to be instructed; social anchoring (“honoured amongst people”) signals editorial present.
Dialogue attribution (“Then the apostle speaks…”) plus institutional categories (elect) and practical promise of answered prayer; not cosmos→cosmos mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: For this entreaty has been since the beginning [...] the gods first made entreaty of their Father. They were granted their entreaty and their request.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the institutional/church graft: references to “the holy church that assumes the flesh…”, and the devotional-Christian linkage “him and the son, the Christ,” which pivots cosmos→church/Christ-language.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens with cosmological antiquity claim (gods entreating the Father) consistent with archetypal myth; then turns to church establishment and Christ wording (later application/overlay).
Rhetorical transition in first-person instruction without cosmological content; functions as editorial teaching scaffolding.

paragraphs.core_text: The Great Spirit, the Mother of Life, she claimed and prayed and besought and glorified and praised the first established one, who is the Father. She besought him an entreaty. She claimed of him a request. She received a great gift; she and the many powers with her.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Archetypal cosmological episode; named emanational beings in systematic mythic action (cosmos→cosmos).

paragraphs.core_text: She besought an entreaty on behalf of the First Man, because of how he had come forth and thrown himself down. He became distant from the Mother of Life. He separated from her and gave himself; in great affliction. He joined war on earth with the destruction and the grief and the weakness; in the worlds of Darkness; in the abysses made of fear; in the midst of the demons' ditch; amongst the powers of the Devil!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmological narrative of the First Man’s descent/war in Darkness; no institutional targeting.

paragraphs.core_text: Indeed, he is like a king standing in the midst of his enemies. And when the Mother of Life petitioned and prayed and glorified and praised the Father, the first established one, she did petition him that he might send a power; a protector and redeemer and helper for the son of God who is set in affliction.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the archetypal supplication logic within the emanational system; “son of God” appears as a cosmic-role epithet here rather than an NT citation.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, just as she had besought and interceded, so likewise was her prayer fulfilled and received into the presence of the Father of Greatness. He turned and gave to her her entreaty: the great power, the Living Spirit, the giver of ease. The Mother of Life and the Living Spirit came with great power to the borders of the territory. They brought the First Man up from that war and struggle, wherein he is set.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic emanational response: Father of Greatness→Living Spirit; impersonal mechanism of rescue (cosmos→cosmos).

paragraphs.core_text: He gave himself as a grace for the Mother of Life. He became estranged and far from her, the one whom his enemies (place) in great affliction, the one who is in the land of Darkness since he became weak.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic plight and estrangement in Darkness; no church-language.

paragraphs.core_text: The Living Spirit grasped and took him in. He freed him. He set him right and gave him ease in the land of rest [...] the Living Spirit, the first giver of ease [...] the will of these three. The welcomer [...] find with the welcomer that [...
paragraphs.temporal_note: Emanational rescue and relocation into “land of rest”; structural cosmology (despite lacunae).

paragraphs.core_text: [...] a great power [...] of the loved one [...] the First Man who had been far away. He had become distant. She had besought on his behalf. He was set fast in affliction. (The Living Spirit) went to the place of destruction and weakness, the one that freed and redeemed him and gave him ease from the affliction. He set him right with rest and joy. He has himself become rested, with him for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the first archetypal “entreaty→rescue→rest” pattern internally to the cosmos.
Didactic recap in first person (“See now, I have taught you…”); functions as editorial structuring rather than substrate exposition.
Explicit pivot to contemporary practice (“faithful saints… over the one who has been released from his body”); cosmos used to authorize church intercession.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] and they built the universe and completed it with its firmaments, with its wheels, with the ships of light that are in the heights, with its fastenings, with its earths and its walls, with its vessels. They completed the universe and set it right by the fathers of light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Constituent parts of the universe listed in cosmological register (firmaments/wheels/ships of light).

paragraphs.core_text: Then, the Great Spirit stood with the Beloved of the Lights, the Great Builder with the Living Spirit and the First Man. These five stood to prayer; they glorified and praised the Father, the first established one. They besought of him an entreaty. They claimed of him a request, that he might give them the power [...] the leader, a guide to all the things of activity that they had constructed. That he might come and purify the living soul that is set in affliction.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second archetypal supplication: enumerated cosmic actors (“these five”) requesting a salvific leader; still cosmos→cosmos.

paragraphs.core_text: They prayed and besought their Father, and he received from them their prayer [...] he gave them their entreaty and their request [...] he summoned from him [...] which is the Third Ambassador. He, he came from the power of his greatness. He saw the entire soul, how it is entangled in a chain and set fast. It sees the things of activity that his brothers have constructed, that have come from the heights. Again, he saw the living soul, that it is entangled and set fast in a great torture. It is oppressed in the stink of the abyss that is joined with it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Emanational grant (Third Ambassador) and diagnosis of the soul’s entanglement; mechanistic cosmology rather than moral exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: And therefore, he, the Ambassador [...] in his charity. So, he revealed his way, before this underworld that is dug deep down, to free the living soul. He redeemed it from all the fleshes of death wherein it is pained. He gave it ease. He set it right in the place of rest and joy.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic descent/way-revelation and extraction of the living soul; “fleshes of death” is mythic-cosmological, not institutional.

paragraphs.core_text: And again, he too, the Ambassador, he fulfilled the will of these three; the will of his brothers who had besought the Father for him. They claimed of him a request, together with the [...] of the Father, the one that [...] he gave the entreaty that they had besought of him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues internal “will/entreaty/request” mechanics among cosmic triads and the Father.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is the transferral of the living soul that he had freed. He released it and gave it ease from the affliction. He became king and first to the entire body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological result statement (“transferral of the living soul”); no church anchoring.
First-person recap marker (“Behold, I have instructed you…”) signals editorial organization of exempla.
Institutional application to “perfect elect… catechumen… prayer in faith”; explicitly cosmos→community practice.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, let us come to the third entreaty when they besought him the third time [...] displayed his image [...] he hid his image from the [...] he stood firm [...] they revealed [...] the light [...] the First Man [...] mock [...] to him in [...] which is exalted [...] garment [...] they were freed [...] to him [...] their voice [...] the body [...] prayer [...] it [...] beseech [...] the body [...] beseech [...] she besought [...] in [...] be free [...] Ambassador [...] and also [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Though highly lacunose, it remains within mythic/cosmic action (image/light/First Man/Ambassador) rather than church discipline.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] with the living ones and [...] for ever [...] the first [...] from the [...] he gave him the hope [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary continuation of the mythic sequence; no institutional markers survive in the readable bits.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, Jesus the Splendour perfected the will [...] the will [...] they found the light [...] the will of the [...] that he had [...] he gave them the power that is Jesus the Splendour. He granted the will of the elements. [...] for ever. This first [...] he was humbled, he was made free [...] the [...]-ness is displayed to his enemies. He received the hope [...] reveal [...] Jesus the Splendour, the light power [...] and the entreaty of the [...] of light [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Jesus the Splendour appears as a defined cosmological power (not an NT citation); the passage stays within emanational will/power/elements.
Present-tense didactic address (“Happen you know this… you are set firm…”) without new cosmological mapping; likely editorial linkage.
Institutional anchor (“petition of the holy church”) in a fragment; cosmos→church language.
Directly about alms/remembrance for the dead; practice-focused rather than cosmological mechanism.

paragraphs.core_text: It is redeemed and purified and attains its first essence.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the intercessory/alms-for-the-dead application frame (“freed by cause of… in the name of that person… beseeches for the soul of the one who has been freed from his body… forgiveness of sins”).

paragraphs.core_text: this is how this soul shall find ease and escape that body. It goes into the land of light [...] soul that was redeemed because of it [...] comes about for it; and it goes to the land of life and rest [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the comparative causal opening (“Just as ease has come about… by cause of this soul”), which rhetorically ties the ascent mechanism to the intercession scenario.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Contains a recognizably old ascent register (escape body; land of Light/life/rest) embedded in a late intercession argument.
